question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 26 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The new UI flow feature flag change led to increased user interaction and higher request volume, causing the p95 latency to rise.
why_chain: The new UI flow feature flag was enabled, increasing user interaction.
Increased user interaction led to higher request volume.
Higher request volume caused the autoscaler to scale out, increasing the number of instances.
More instances did not scale the latency down as expected, leading to a rise in p95 latency.

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign went live, causing a sudden increase in user activity.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign went live, increasing user activity.
Increased user activity led to higher request volume.
Higher request volume caused the autoscaler to scale out, increasing the number of instances.
More instances did not scale the latency down as expected, leading to a rise in p95 latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of search v3.1 caused the increase in p95 latency.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment was routine and occurred hours before the change, not at the right time and place.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The autoscaler scaling out was the cause of the p95 latency increase.
ruled_out.reason: The autoscaler scaling out occurred after the change, not at the right time and place.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region eu-west rose from 137 ms to 224 ms (+64%), with a change point at 2026-03-26T13:45:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region eu-west: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for region eu-west rose (2118 per 5 min before, 7734 per 5 min after, +265%).
At the same time, error rate for region eu-west rose (0.48% before, 0.97% after, +102%).
Changed checkout feature flag new_ui_flow to 50% in eu-west (checkout, eu-west; 3 min before the change; record R016; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in eu-west at 13:45 UTC (eu-west; 220 min before the change; record R014; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
Request volume 3x normal in eu-west (eu-west; 12 min after the change; record R017; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed search v3.1 to eu-west (routine release) (search, eu-west; 136 min before the change; record R015; fit: hours before the change, too early to explain a sudden jump)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (eu-west; 20 min after the change; record R018; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (3 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✗ Request volume also rose, so a traffic explanation is still open.
✗ 1 other change event(s) fit about as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
✗ Two or more changes fit equally well, so the cause cannot be confirmed.
missing_data: Details to tell the competing changes apart (e.g. a rollback test)

actions.action: Roll back the new UI flow feature flag change to eu-west.
Monitor for similar campaigns and prepare a rollback plan if a similar campaign goes live.
Review and optimize the autoscaler configuration for eu-west.
